transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Hello, Doctor. Well, my daughter wanted me to come talk to you because... well, she says I never sit still, and I suppose she's right. I feel like I’m always up and moving. Even on a quiet day when I'm supposed to be relaxing, I’m bouncing from the garden club list to my knitting bag to digging out old travel papers before I’ve really finished any one thing. 

Which reminds me, I was looking through those travel papers because I wanted to find the itinerary from our Alaska cruise. We went a few years ago and it was just spectacular. Have you ever been? They served this baked Alaska dessert on the ship, which I always thought was a bit of a cliché, but it was actually delicious. I tried to make it at home once for my grandson's birthday, but the meringue didn't set right at all. I think it was too humid that day, or maybe my oven runs a little hot. I've been meaning to have the repairman look at it, but he charges a fortune just to come out to the house... 

I'm sorry, what was I saying? Oh, right, why I'm here. Yes, just always on the go, I suppose.
Have you noticed any recent problems with your memory?

Memory? Oh, well, no, I wouldn't say my memory is bad. I mean, I can remember all sorts of things. Just the other day, I was telling my daughter about the time we went to the state fair when she was a little girl. She must have been about seven, maybe eight? She had this bright pink cotton candy, and it got all in her hair. It was a nightmare to wash out, let me tell you. We had to use that special shampoo, the one in the yellow bottle... what was it called? Johnson's, I think. Do they still make that? I haven't bought baby shampoo in ages. 

My grandson uses this fancy organic stuff now that costs an arm and a leg. His mother buys it online. I tried to order some things online once, some knitting yarn, but the website was so confusing. All these buttons and pop-ups. I ended up calling the company instead. The woman on the phone was very nice, though. She lived in Ohio, and we had a lovely chat about the weather. It was snowing there, but here it was just raining. I hate the rain, it makes my knees ache. 

But anyway, no, my memory is fine. I just... I just have a lot on my mind, I suppose.
Have you had this restless, easily distracted way of being since you were a child?

Oh, goodness, yes. I suppose I have. Even back in grade school, my teachers used to tell my mother that I was bright but just so scattered. I was always losing my school papers, talking out of turn, and wiggling around in my seat before I’d even finished my work. 

My third-grade teacher, Mrs. Gable, she used to get so frustrated with me. She was a very stern woman, always wore these heavy wool skirts, even in the spring. I don't know how she didn't just melt! I can't stand wool against my skin, it makes me itch terribly. I have to buy all my sweaters in cotton or those nice bamboo blends they make now. Have you felt those? They're incredibly soft. My daughter bought me a beautiful pale blue one for Christmas last year, wrapped it in this gorgeous silver paper with a big velvet bow. I always save the bows from presents, you know, because you can just stick a bit of tape on the back and use them again next year. It seems so wasteful to throw them away, especially the nice fabric ones. My husband used to tease me about my big box of recycled bows in the closet... 

Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, childhood! Yes, I was quite the wiggly little girl, always losing things and talking too much.
